recommendations.title: RESOLVED (root cause confirmed) -- Aug 21-23 LPV surge was a rotating multi-language Dailypush push campaign, not a bug or bot traffic (Aug 24: blended conversion still ~20.5%, consistent, not independently re-verified this refresh)
recommendations.finding: The LPV surge flagged urgently in the prior refresh (LPV 358,574 -> 578,672 -> 731,170 over Aug 20-22, then reversing to 534,921 on Aug 23, with LPV->Lead-Created conversion compressing from 24.5% to 20.7-21.7% and NOT recovering when volume dropped on Aug 23) has been traced to its cause: postpaid_acq_Dailypush, a push-notification campaign, began firing large single-language-targeted batches -- Hindi drove 194,959 LPV (39.0% of total) on Aug 21; five languages (Gujarati, Kannada, Telugu, Bengali, Tamil) fired on the SAME day, Aug 22, totaling 389,989 LPV (53.3% of that day's peak total -- this 5-language pileup is specifically what produced the Aug 22 peak); English drove 208,483 LPV (39.0% of total) on Aug 23. The Dailypush family's own conversion held at a consistent 15.0-19.1% across every day in the window, while non-Dailypush conversion held rock-steady at 25.4-25.9% across the same days (backed out by subtracting Dailypush LPV/leads from the daily total). The blended-rate compression is fully explained as a traffic-mix effect: Dailypush's share of daily LPV grew from 8.5% (Aug 20) to 39-55% (Aug 21-23), pulling the BLENDED average down even though non-push funnel performance never changed. This rules out both hypotheses raised in the prior refresh (bot/crawler traffic, tracking double-fire) -- it is real, identifiable campaign activity. UPDATE (2026-08-25 refresh): LPV->Lead-Created held at 20.51% on Aug 24 (20.58% on Aug 23), consistent with Dailypush continuing to run at an elevated share of daily volume -- but this was NOT independently re-confirmed this cycle, since the campaign-level breakdown query for Aug 24 hit Trino's 'too many queued queries' saturation (see campaign_traffic stale_note). Treat the root cause as established, not the Aug 24 continuation specifically -- re-verify the campaign split next refresh once Trino has headroom.
recommendations.expected_impact: No underlying funnel-health issue exists -- non-push conversion has not moved. Two follow-ups remain, neither urgent in the 'something is broken' sense the prior refresh flagged: (1) confirm with growth/marketing whether firing 5 language-variant push batches on a single calendar day (Aug 22) was an intentional scheduling decision -- it produced a ~2x volume spike with real downstream load implications (BRE/lender API call volume roughly doubled that day), worth knowing about even if intentional; (2) the core dashboard's headline conversion KPI is vulnerable to this kind of mix-shift masking a stable (or even improving) underlying funnel as a false regression -- worth adding a campaign-tier or paid/push-vs-organic split to the Overview page's KPIs, not just the Campaign Traffic detail page, so this doesn't read as a false alarm again next time a large push campaign runs.

recommendations.title: Escalate the SSFB Aadhaar/eKYC vendor timeout — the single largest, best-evidenced CHRONIC leak in the funnel
recommendations.finding: KYC In Progress converts only ~51-56% of Aadhaar-OTP customers on every normal day (excluding the now-resolved Aug 18 outage) across the full Aug 1-20 window — a chronic loss, not a one-off. Independently confirmed via Elasticsearch: error code LOS-NEXUS-EXT-11002 (SSFB Aadhaar vendor 504 timeout) fires thousands of times daily against exactly this API call. Two independent sources agree on both location and persistence.
recommendations.expected_impact: Recovering even 10pp of this stage's conversion would carry roughly 3,000-3,500 more customers/day past KYC In Progress at current volumes — the single highest-leverage STRUCTURAL fix available in this funnel, since every downstream stage from here converts at 80%+.

recommendations.title: Investigate whether the BRE1 Success drop (~30-34% conversion) is credit decisioning or a UX/drop-off issue — don't fix blind
recommendations.finding: BRE1 Success remains the second-largest leak, stable day to day (30.5%-33.7% across Aug 12-20, 31.5% on Aug 20). Elasticsearch shows CreateBRELead API failures at only dozens-to-low-hundreds per day — nowhere near large enough to explain a gap this size. That rules OUT API errors as the primary driver but does NOT establish the real one: genuine credit-policy rejection (not a 'bug') vs. UX/comprehension drop-off before the BRE decision completes. Needs a proper /investigate, not a guess.
recommendations.expected_impact: Unknown until investigated — but given the volume at this stage (30-40K customers/day reach BRE1 Requested), even a modest recoverable fraction would be the second-largest structural lever in the funnel after the KYC fix above.

pan_prefill.definition: Rate = COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id WHERE event_action='pan-card-pan-prefilled') / LPV (same day/range). 'no_pan_event' = LPV customers with neither a prefilled nor not-prefilled event that day (approximate -- a customer firing both events is counted once in each bucket, so this is a ceiling, not exact).

prefill_source.correction_note: 2026-08-14: PM flagged our original CACHE/SIGNZY reading as wrong -- that came from FETCH_PAN_INFO/ToolsService, a PAN *validation* lookup, not prefill sourcing. Corrected to the actual prefill-source field: panSource, embedded per-field in PrefillingService's response payload.
prefill_source.operation: PrefillingService: fetchPrefillingData: response (operation FETCH_PREFILLING, product_type loc)
prefill_source.field: panSource, read from the JSON payload at context.domain['postpaid-bff'].details. When PAN wasn't prefilled, panSource is simply absent from the payload (bucketed as NOT_PREFILLED here, not a missing-data gap).
prefill_source.index_pattern: lending-postpaid-bff-fe-prod_indexer_YYYY-MM-DD (queried as a wildcard across days, not a single day-index -- see day_boundary_gotcha)
prefill_source.day_boundary_gotcha: The per-day index name is not IST-aligned, so querying a single day's index alone undercounts vs. the true IST calendar day. Confirmed live 2026-08-14: querying index lending-postpaid-bff-fe-prod_indexer_2026-08-12 alone returned 64,062 matching docs; a date_histogram with time_zone Asia/Kolkata across the wildcard pattern for the same IST calendar day returned 136,527. Always use the IST-corrected date_histogram approach in prefill_source_query.md, never a single day-index directly.
prefill_source.sources_note: CIF and KYB are the two real upstream services that can supply prefill data (customer information file lookup vs. KYB/vendor-sourced data). NOT_PREFILLED means the field was genuinely absent from the response -- the user has to enter PAN manually. No other panSource value has been observed as of 2026-08-14; re-run the source-enumeration sample periodically in case a new value appears.

pattern_findings.finding: ROOT CAUSE FOUND for the Aug 21-23 LPV surge/reversal flagged in the prior refresh's top recommendation. postpaid_acq_Dailypush -- previously a modest campaign (~14-30k LPV/day, 8.5% of total LPV on Aug 20) -- began firing large, single-language-targeted batches: postpaid_acq_Dailypush_Hindi_AllBase alone drove 194,959 LPV on Aug 21 (39.0% of that day's total). On Aug 22, FIVE language variants fired on the SAME day -- Gujarati (90,502), Kannada (88,104), Telugu (79,128), Bengali (70,539), Tamil (60,716), summing to 389,989 LPV (53.3% of that day's 731,170 total) -- this 5-language pileup is specifically what produced Aug 22's peak. On Aug 23, English_AllBase alone drove 208,483 LPV (39.0% of that day's 534,921 total). Aggregating the whole Dailypush family by day: LPV share of total funnel traffic went 08-20: 8.5% -> 08-21: 39.0% -> 08-22: 55.0% -> 08-23: 41.3%, while the campaign's own conversion held at 15.0-19.1% every single day (08-19: 19.1%, 08-20: 9.5%, 08-21: 15.0%, 08-22: 17.0%, 08-23: 15.0%) -- consistently far below the non-Dailypush conversion rate, which stayed rock-steady at 25.4-25.9% across the identical window. The blended LPV->Lead-Created compression from 24.5% to 20.7-21.7% flagged previously is therefore a pure traffic-mix effect: a large, low-intent push-notification segment did not degrade underlying funnel performance -- it diluted the blended average because it got much bigger. This is real, identifiable campaign activity, not a bot/crawler or a tracking double-fire (both hypotheses raised in the prior refresh are now ruled out).
pattern_findings.recommendation: Confirm with growth/marketing whether firing 5 language batches on the same calendar day (Aug 22) was an intentional scheduling choice or a batching collision -- it produced a highly irregular ~2x volume spike with real downstream load implications (BRE/lender API call volume roughly doubled that day). Separately, this is now a strong case for splitting headline funnel KPIs by acquisition channel/campaign-tier so a large push campaign's inherently lower conversion doesn't read as a funnel-health regression the next time this recurs -- see the rewritten top Recommendation.

incident_finding.title: Recurring resolver/lead-creation outage: 2026-08-03, 2026-08-06, and 2026-08-18 -- confirmed fully resolved as of 2026-08-20
incident_finding.finding: Resolver-controller failures ("Failed to fetch user journey from resolver controller") have now spiked to outage scale THREE times in the tracked window: 167,656 distinct customers on 2026-08-03, 28,669 on 2026-08-06, and 20,662 on 2026-08-18 -- all far above the ~26-130/day baseline seen on every other day. Each of the three spike days has a corroborating spike in lead create/update failures the same day (1,876 on 08-03, 558 on 08-06, 3,764 on 08-18 -- notably the LARGEST lead-update spike of the three even though 08-18's resolver spike was the smallest of the three, so the two signatures don't scale perfectly proportionally with each other). The FETCH_PAN_INFO/PAN-validation signature stayed comparatively flat on all three days (1,329, 1,504, and 1,932 respectively -- a modest 08-18 bump, not remotely spike-scale), continuing to sharpen the root cause to the resolver/lead-creation path specifically, not a PAN-vendor issue. UPDATE (2026-08-20 refresh): the 2026-08-18 spike did not cut off sharply -- 2026-08-19 showed a declining residual (resolver-controller: 2,385 vs the 20,662 peak; lead-update: 553 vs the 3,764 peak), and by 2026-08-20 (partial day) both signatures were back near baseline (346 and 11 respectively). Total customer-days of elevated impact for this occurrence: at least 2 full days (08-18 peak + 08-19 tail). CONFIRMED RESOLVED (2026-08-21 refresh): 2026-08-20 is now a complete day showing resolver-controller at 432 and lead-update at 11 -- both at/near the pre-incident baseline. The 08-18 spike's full lifecycle is now on record: 20,662 (peak, 08-18) -> 2,385 (08-19) -> 432 (08-20), a clean ~10x-per-day decay, not a second wave or plateau.
incident_finding.root_cause: Same signature confirmed on 2026-08-18 as the original 08-03 finding: refCode UE-BFFAXIOS-ERROR-NEXUSSERVICE, calling out to nexusService (workflow-nexus), with sampled raw documents showing ~30,000ms latency (a 30-second timeout) and HTTP 417/500 responses, spread across distinct customers, devices, and campaigns at different times of day (00:38, 03:17, 14:21 IST sampled on 08-18) -- not a single retrying customer (retry-inflation ruled out per anomaly-methodology.md's standard check). This is consistent with workflow-nexus itself being unavailable or severely degraded for one or more periods on each of the three dates.
incident_finding.confidence: HIGH for root cause pattern (corroborated across 2 independent error signatures on all 3 occurrence days, uniform ~30s-timeout signature). MEDIUM on actual funnel impact -- see the cross-check below, which found no clear aggregate conversion drop on 08-18 despite the error volume.
incident_finding.recommendation: Escalate as a RECURRING P1 with the workflow-nexus/backend team -- three occurrences (08-03, 08-06, 08-18) with the identical signature is a pattern, not an isolated event. Since the 08-18 occurrence is now fully resolved with no ongoing impact, the ask is purely recurrence-prevention: whether there's a common trigger (deploy cadence, downstream dependency, traffic threshold) across all three dates, since none of the three fall on an obviously shared day-of-week or date pattern.

insight_cards.text: 20.5108% on Aug 24, essentially flat with Aug 22/23 (20.8%/20.7%), still well below the 24.6-26.5% band held through Aug 20. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED this cycle: the postpaid_acq_Dailypush push campaign fired large single-language batches Aug 21-23 (up to 55% of a day's total LPV on Aug 22) at a consistent 15.0-19.1% own conversion, far below the 25.4-25.9% non-Dailypush rate held steady the whole time. The blended-average compression is a pure mix-shift, not a funnel regression -- both hypotheses raised previously (bot/crawler traffic, tracking double-fire) are ruled out.
insight_cards.recommendation: No funnel fix needed. Confirm with growth/marketing whether stacking 5 language variants on Aug 22 was intentional, and add a campaign-tier/paid-vs-organic split to the Overview KPIs so a large push campaign's inherently lower conversion doesn't read as a false regression next time.
